description:
README.md:222-227 has a Features table:

    | Feature | Enables |
    |---------|---------|
    | `crl` | `CrlChecker` (offline CRL validation, with delta CRL support) |
    | `ocsp` | `OcspChecker` (offline OCSP validation) |
    | `rsa` | RSA-PKCS1v15 backend in `DefaultVerifier` (default on) |
    | `p256` | ECDSA P-256 backend in `DefaultVerifier` (default on) |

But pkix-chain's Cargo.toml declares only these features:

    default     = [\"pkix-path/default\"]
    rustcrypto  = [\"pkix-path/rustcrypto\"]
    crl         = [\"pkix-revocation/crl\"]
    ocsp        = [\"pkix-revocation/ocsp\"]
    serde       = [...]

A caller running `cargo add pkix-chain --features rsa` will get a hard
error from cargo: \"the package `pkix-chain` does not contain a feature
named `rsa`\". Same for `p256`.

`rsa` and `p256` are features of the upstream `pkix-path` crate, and
the `rustcrypto` / `default` features in pkix-chain transitively pull
them in via `pkix-path/default`. But they are not callable as
pkix-chain features.

The Features table also omits the `rustcrypto` and `serde` features
that pkix-chain actually does declare.

Suggested fix: rewrite the table to match Cargo.toml. Either drop the
rsa/p256 rows entirely, or document the transitive activation pattern
explicitly:

    | pkix-chain feature | Effect |
    |--------------------|--------|
    | `default` | Pulls `pkix-path/default` (RSA-PKCS1v15-SHA-256 + ECDSA-P-256) |
    | `rustcrypto` | Pulls `pkix-path/rustcrypto` (all RustCrypto backends) |
    | `crl` | Enables `CrlChecker` (offline CRL) |
    | `ocsp` | Enables `OcspChecker` (offline OCSP) |
    | `serde` | Derives Serialize / Deserialize on Error and friends |

Caller impact: anyone reading the README to decide what to enable.
title: README Features table lists rsa and p256 as pkix-chain features; they do not exist
